title: Historical V54 - Example Workflows
summary: Practical workflows for learning the runtime through safe, inspectable requests.
html:
Historical reference. See the current V55 architecture guide before using this material.

Example Workflows

These examples are meant to exercise the runtime without requiring risky changes.

Inspect A Repository

Summarize this repository structure and identify the main FastAPI entry points.

Expected behavior:

  • source inspection;
  • no file mutation;
  • route and package summary;
  • optional generated table or DisplayDocument.

Produce A Local Report

Create a short Markdown report about Python files changed most recently and save it as artifacts/source-report.md.

Expected behavior:

  • approval before writing;
  • command or Python action capsule;
  • verification that the file exists;
  • final response with path.

Schedule A Reminder

Remind me tomorrow morning to review the gateway logs.

Expected behavior:

  • event draft;
  • timezone handling;
  • saved runtime event;
  • future execution through the same pipeline.

Debug A Gateway

Check whether the local gateway is healthy and explain any failure without changing files.

Expected behavior:

  • health probe;
  • no mutation;
  • concise diagnosis;
  • gateway metadata in trace or capsule.

Review Email Without Mutating It

In my primary Gmail account, summarize security alerts from the last 30 days.

Expected behavior:

  • account-scoped Gmail search;
  • local metadata cache use where possible;
  • bounded selected-message or selected-thread context;
  • no send, trash, archive, or label mutation.

Draft A Gmail Reply

Draft a short reply to the selected email saying I will review it tomorrow.

Expected behavior:

  • selected-thread context only;
  • editable draft text;
  • no send until the user explicitly asks and approves;
  • trace details showing Gmail account and draft state.
